AcceptedJobResponse.description:
Returned by endpoints that hand work to Celery (sections 35, 77).

The client polls ``status_url`` instead of holding a long request open.
AcceptedJobResponse.title: AcceptedJobResponse

AccessTokenResponse.description: Browser-visible half of a token pair; never contains a refresh secret.
AccessTokenResponse.title: AccessTokenResponse

AcknowledgedResult.description:
Deliberately contentless.

The password-reset endpoints answer identically whether or not the address
belongs to an account, so there is nothing here that could differ between
the two cases (section 38).
AcknowledgedResult.title: AcknowledgedResult

AddressCreate.description:
A billing or shipping address.

``state_code`` is optional in the schema but mandatory in the database for a
domestic address; the service reports that as a business-rule error naming
the field rather than letting a constraint violation surface as a 500.
AddressCreate.title: AddressCreate

AddressType.description:
What an address is used for.

Kept to the two that change a document: the billing address determines the
GSTIN and place of supply on the invoice, the shipping address determines
where the consignment physically goes and which state code the e-way bill
carries. A "registered office" nobody ever raises a document against is a
note, not an address type.
AddressType.title: AddressType

AddressUpdate.description:
Partial update of an address.

``address_type`` cannot be changed: a billing address that becomes a
shipping address would have to renegotiate the single-default rule for two
types at once, and the operation is indistinguishable from creating the
address you actually meant.
AddressUpdate.title: AddressUpdate

AdjustmentReason.description:
Why stock is being written up or down.

Mandatory on every adjustment: section 83 requires a reason for every
movement, and "someone adjusted it" is not one. The vocabulary is closed so
the write-off report can group by cause.
AdjustmentReason.title: AdjustmentReason

AgeingCurrencyBlock.description:
One denomination's ageing: its parties, and what they add up to.

A block is the unit in which this report is arithmetically meaningful. Every
figure in it is in :attr:`currency`, and nothing in it was added to a figure
from another block - there is no exchange rate in this schema with which
that could have been done honestly.
AgeingCurrencyBlock.title: AgeingCurrencyBlock

AgeingReport.description:
Ageing per denomination, with one of them restated at the top level.

Multi-currency is an open question for this business (``docs/assumptions.md``,
open question 3) and there is no exchange-rate table to convert with. Two
failures follow from that, and this shape is built to avoid both:

* A total that adds rupees to dollars means nothing, and ranking parties by
  it is worse than meaningless. So every total lives inside an
  :class:`AgeingCurrencyBlock` and no figure anywhere spans two.
* A report narrowed to one denomination tells a company whose debts are all
  in another that it owes nothing. So :attr:`currencies` carries *every*
  denomination with an open item - narrowing is a choice about what to
  restate at the top, never about what the report covers.

:attr:`currency` and the ``rows``/``total_*`` fields beside it are the
primary block - ``currencies[0]`` - repeated at the top level so the
single-currency company this system is built for today reads the answer
without walking a list. They are a restatement, not a second figure.
AgeingReport.title: AgeingReport

AgeingRow.description:
One party's outstanding split across the ageing buckets.

Every figure is in :attr:`currency`, which is the currency of the block the
row belongs to: a row is a set of sums, and this schema has no exchange rate
with which to add one denomination to another. The same party appears once
per denomination it owes in, never once with the two added together.
AgeingRow.title: AgeingRow

AllocationRequest.description:
Settle invoices from an approved payment.

``replace`` decides whether the given allocations are added to what the
payment already carries or replace it entirely. Defaulting to False makes a
retried request additive rather than destructive only if the caller says so.
AllocationRequest.title: AllocationRequest

ApprovalDecisionRequest.description:
Body of ``POST /audit/approvals/{id}/approve`` and ``.../reject``.

One shape for both decisions so the note is validated identically; whether a
note is *required* depends on the decision and is therefore a service rule,
not a schema rule.
ApprovalDecisionRequest.title: ApprovalDecisionRequest

ApprovalRequest.description: Reason and optional note captured when a vendor is approved or blocked.
ApprovalRequest.title: ApprovalRequest

ApprovalRequestRead.description:
One row of the approval queue.

``can_decide`` and ``blocked_reason`` are computed per caller, which is why
this model is built through :meth:`from_model` rather than validated straight
off the ORM object: the same row is decidable by one user and not by another.
ApprovalRequestRead.title: ApprovalRequestRead

ApprovalStatus.description:
Lifecycle of an :class:`~src.modules.audit.models.ApprovalRequest`.

Declared here rather than on the model because the model stores the column as
``String(24)`` and belongs to the recording half of this module, which must
not change. The set of strings is nonetheless part of the API contract, so it
belongs with the other contract types.
ApprovalStatus.title: ApprovalStatus

AssemblyOrderDetail.description:
Header plus its component set.

Not paginated, by deliberate exception to section 31: the component set is
bounded by ``MAX_COMPONENTS_PER_ORDER`` at write time and a kitting list is
only meaningful whole.
AssemblyOrderDetail.title: AssemblyOrderDetail

AssemblyOrderStatus.description:
Lifecycle of an assembly order (master rules section 19).

``CANCELLED`` is reachable only before the components have been issued.
Once parts are on the bench and reserved against the order, the way out is
to complete it (possibly with everything rejected) or to close it after
returning the parts - cancelling would leave reservations belonging to a
document that claims never to have existed.

``QC_PENDING`` sits between assembly and completion for outputs that need
inspecting. The stock exists by then, but on QC hold rather than available.
AssemblyOrderStatus.title: AssemblyOrderStatus

AssemblyOrderUpdate.description:
Amend a draft.

Only a DRAFT is editable: past approval the order has been committed to a
schedule and, from RELEASED, to stock. ``item_id`` and ``bom_id`` are absent
on purpose - changing what is being built is a different order, not an edit,
because the exploded component set would no longer match the header.
AssemblyOrderUpdate.title: AssemblyOrderUpdate

AssemblySourceType.description:
What demand this assembly order was raised to cover.

Read the same way procurement reads its own source pair: two orders naming
the same source demand are covering the same shortage twice.
AssemblySourceType.title: AssemblySourceType

AuditAction.description: The action vocabulary from master rules section 41.
AuditAction.title: AuditAction

AuditLogListItem.description:
One row of the audit feed.

Carries ``changed_fields`` - a short list of column names - but not the
before/after values themselves. That is what makes a page of this shape cheap
enough to be the default listing; ``GET /audit/logs/{id}`` returns the values.
AuditLogListItem.title: AuditLogListItem

AuditLogRead.description: One audit entry in full, including the before/after diff.
AuditLogRead.title: AuditLogRead

AuthenticatedUser.description: The minimum a client needs to render a shell after sign-in.
AuthenticatedUser.title: AuthenticatedUser

AvailabilityRead.description: Answer to "how much can I promise?" - never served from cache (section 34).
AvailabilityRead.title: AvailabilityRead

AvailableToPromiseRead.description:
What can still be promised for one item.

Read from the balance table on every call and never cached (section 34): a
stale "yes, we have it" turns into a delivery date the company cannot meet.
AvailableToPromiseRead.title: AvailableToPromiseRead

BlockRequest.description: Put an account on credit hold.
BlockRequest.title: BlockRequest

BomCreate.description:
Payload for a new BOM.

``company_id`` is absent by design - it comes from the authenticated
principal (master rules section 40). ``code`` is absent too: it is issued
from the document sequence so two engineers creating a BOM at the same
moment cannot be given the same one.
BomCreate.title: BomCreate

BomDetail.description: One BOM with its lines and operations, loaded in two batched queries.
BomDetail.title: BomDetail

BomLineIn.description: One component on a create or update payload.
BomLineIn.title: BomLineIn

BomOperationIn.description: One costed routing step on a create or update payload.
BomOperationIn.title: BomOperationIn

BomStatus.description:
Lifecycle of one BOM version (database.md section 5).

Only ``APPROVED`` structures are visible to planning. ``OBSOLETE`` is
terminal: a superseded structure is retained because documents raised
against it still reference it.
BomStatus.title: BomStatus

BomStatusChange.description:
Reason capture for a lifecycle transition.

Required, not optional: master rules section 83. A structure that went
obsolete for no recorded reason is unanswerable six months later.
BomStatusChange.title: BomStatusChange

BomSummary.description: List row. Deliberately without lines - the grid does not render them.
BomSummary.title: BomSummary

BomType.description:
What the structure is used for.

``PHANTOM`` is the one with explosion semantics attached: a phantom is a
drawing-level grouping that is never stocked, so the explosion blows through
it and raises requirements for its children only (master rules section 11).
``ALTERNATE`` marks a structure that exists beside a default one - it carries
``parent_bom_id`` pointing at the BOM it is an alternative to.
BomType.title: BomType

BomUpdate.description:
Partial update of a DRAFT BOM.

``item_id`` and ``version`` are absent: both are identity. Re-pointing a BOM
at a different item would break the composite foreign key that keeps
``bom_lines.parent_item_id`` honest, and a version is created by copying,
never by editing.

``lines`` and ``operations`` are wholesale replacements when present. A
per-line patch protocol would need its own concurrency story on top of the
row version, for a screen that submits the whole grid anyway.
BomUpdate.title: BomUpdate

BulkIgnoreRequest.description: Dismiss several suggestions at once, with one shared reason.
BulkIgnoreRequest.title: BulkIgnoreRequest

BulkIgnoreResult.description:
Outcome of a bulk dismissal.

``skipped`` is reported rather than raising: a planner selecting a page of
suggestions where one has already been converted should not have the whole
action refused, but must be told which ones were left alone.
BulkIgnoreResult.title: BulkIgnoreResult

CartonContentIn.description:
One quantity of one item going into a carton.

``serial_ids`` is required for a serial-tracked item and refused for every
other one: a serial identifies a single physical unit, so the count has to
equal the quantity, and a non-serialised part has nothing to name. The
quantity/count agreement is checked in the service, where the item's
tracking mode is known.
CartonContentIn.title: CartonContentIn

CartonContentsReplace.description:
Replace the whole content set of an open carton.

Replacement rather than append: the packed quantities on the order's lines
are maintained from these rows, and reconciling a partial edit against them
is where an off-by-one becomes a customer receiving the wrong box.
CartonContentsReplace.title: CartonContentsReplace

CartonCreate.description:
Open a new carton on the bench.

``carton_number`` and ``barcode`` are absent: both are assigned by the
server. The number is the next one for this order and the barcode is derived
from it, so a client cannot reserve either.
CartonCreate.title: CartonCreate

CartonDetail.description:
A carton and everything in it.

Contents are not paginated, by the same exception as the order's lines: the
set is bounded by ``MAX_CONTENTS_PER_CARTON`` at write time, and half a
carton's contents is not a useful answer to anybody.
CartonDetail.title: CartonDetail

CartonLabel.description:
Everything a label printer needs, and nothing it does not.

This is the *payload*, not the artwork. Rendering it - to a 100x150 mm
thermal label, to a PDF, to ZPL - is the printer's job; generating pixels in
the request cycle is what section 22 forbids. ``symbology`` is stated
explicitly so a printer does not have to guess how to encode ``barcode``.
CartonLabel.title: CartonLabel

CartonLabelLine.description: One printed line of a carton label's content block.
CartonLabelLine.title: CartonLabelLine

CartonType.description:
Physical form of the outer pack.

ASSUMPTION: the contract does not fix this vocabulary. These are the forms a
hardware manufacturer actually ships in. The value is descriptive - it drives
the label and the freight paperwork, and no rule in this module branches on
it - so extending the list is a one-line change here plus the CHECK below.
CartonType.title: CartonType

ChangePasswordResult.description: ``revoked_sessions`` tells the UI how many other devices were signed out.
ChangePasswordResult.title: ChangePasswordResult

CloseResult.description: Closure, with the costing it computed and froze.
CloseResult.title: CloseResult

CompanyRead.description: The caller's own company. There is no endpoint that reads another one.
CompanyRead.title: CompanyRead

CompanyUpdate.description:
Partial update of the caller's own company.

Two fields are deliberately absent:

``code``       identifies the tenant in exported data and integration
               payloads; renaming it in place would orphan history that has
               already left the building.
``is_active``  deactivating the tenant from inside the tenant would lock
               every user out with no way back in. It is a platform
               operation, not a self-service one.
CompanyUpdate.title: CompanyUpdate

ComparisonItemRow.description: One row of the side-by-side: one item, every vendor's offer for it.
ComparisonItemRow.title: ComparisonItemRow

ComparisonOffer.description: One vendor's offer for one item, priced for comparison.
ComparisonOffer.title: ComparisonOffer

ComparisonVendorColumn.description: One vendor's column header: the totals a buyer compares at a glance.
ComparisonVendorColumn.title: ComparisonVendorColumn

CompletionResult.description: What completion actually posted, so the caller does not have to guess.
CompletionResult.title: CompletionResult

ComponentConsumptionIn.description:
The serialised units one component contributed to this assembly.

Required for every serial-tracked component and rejected for every other
one: a serial identifies a single physical unit, so the count has to equal
the quantity consumed, and a non-serialised part has nothing to name.
ComponentConsumptionIn.title: ComponentConsumptionIn

ComponentIssueIn.description:
Override how much of one component is handed to the line.

Omitting a line issues its full ``required_quantity``, which is the normal
case. An explicit quantity exists for the kitting reality of topping a line
up beyond the recipe, or of issuing short because the rest arrives later.
ComponentIssueIn.title: ComponentIssueIn

ComponentRead.description:
One snapshotted requirement with its live coverage.

``reserved_quantity`` and ``available_quantity`` are read from allocation and
inventory at request time rather than stored: a stored copy would be stale
the moment anybody else moved the part, and availability is never cached
(master rules section 34).
ComponentRead.title: ComponentRead

ComponentShortage.description:
One component the release could not fully cover.

Reported rather than raised: a planner needs the whole list of what is
missing, not the first thing that failed.
ComponentShortage.title: ComponentShortage

ConfirmResult.description: The confirm response: the order, plus what could actually be reserved.
ConfirmResult.title: ConfirmResult

ConversionRequest.description:
A typed instruction to create one document from one suggestion.

This is the seam between planning and execution. When the owning module is
deployed the service hands it this payload and receives back the document it
created; when it is not, the same payload is returned to the caller so the
request can be replayed later or actioned by hand. Either way the *shape* of
what MRP asks for is fixed here rather than being re-derived by each consumer.
ConversionRequest.title: ConversionRequest

ConversionResult.description: Answer to "how much is X FROM in TO?".
ConversionResult.title: ConversionResult

ConversionTarget.description:
The document class a suggestion is turned into.

One target per suggestion type, with the planner free to override: deciding
to buy a part the item master says is made here is a legitimate commercial
call, and ``docs/assumptions.md`` section 6 already accepts that every
suggestion is reviewed before it becomes a transaction. The override is
recorded in the audit entry.
ConversionTarget.title: ConversionTarget

CostCentreCreate.description:
Payload for opening a cost centre.

``cost_centre_type`` is required rather than defaulted: it is how the centre
is grouped on every report, and a silent default would misclassify each one
nobody remembered to change.
CostCentreCreate.title: CostCentreCreate

CostCentreType.description:
How a cost centre is classified on a report. Nothing may branch on it.

The same rule as ``items.item_group``: a reporting classification, never a
switch. A rule that needs to know whether a centre is "production" reads
the carrier it is attached to (a work centre, a production order), not this
column - otherwise reclassifying a centre would silently change behaviour.
CostCentreType.title: CostCentreType

CostCentreUpdate.description:
Partial update. ``code`` is immutable: it is quoted on posted history.

An explicit null clears ``parent_id`` (the centre becomes a root),
``plant_id``, ``head_user_id`` or ``description``; an omitted key is left
alone.
CostCentreUpdate.title: CostCentreUpdate

CreditStatus.description: The answer to "can this account take another order of X?".
CreditStatus.title: CreditStatus

CursorPagination.description: Keyset pagination metadata for very large tables (ledger, audit log).
CursorPagination.title: CursorPagination

CustomerAdjustmentCreate.description:
A debit or credit note against a customer's account, posted by hand.

Nothing here names the receivable account: the receivable leg is always the
system control account, so a caller cannot post a "receivable" adjustment to
an account the ageing report does not read. ``account_id`` is the other leg -
the revenue, expense or write-off account the adjustment belongs to.
CustomerAdjustmentCreate.title: CustomerAdjustmentCreate

CustomerAdjustmentRead.description: What one adjustment did: the journal it posted and the balance it left.
CustomerAdjustmentRead.title: CustomerAdjustmentRead

CustomerAdjustmentType.description:
Which way a manual posting against a customer's account moves the balance.

A Python-side vocabulary for ``POST /finance/customer-adjustments``; the
ledger rows it produces are ordinary entries with ``reference_type``
``customer_adjustment``, so no column carries this value.
CustomerAdjustmentType.title: CustomerAdjustmentType

CustomerCreate.description: Payload for creating a customer, dealer, distributor or OEM account.

credit_limit.description: Maximum exposure allowed. Omit or send null for an unlimited limit; send 0 to forbid credit entirely.
credit_limit.title: Credit Limit

price_list_type.description: Which item_prices.price_type applies to this account.

CustomerCreate.title: CustomerCreate

CustomerDetail.description: Single-customer view, including its addresses and contacts.
CustomerDetail.title: CustomerDetail

CustomerSummary.description:
List row. Deliberately narrower than the detail model - a customer grid
renders none of the address or contact data, and loading it would cost a
join per page for nothing.
CustomerSummary.title: CustomerSummary

CustomerType.description:
Commercial channel the account belongs to.

A classification for reporting, defaults and permission scoping - never a
switch that decides whether an operation is legal. What the account is
charged is decided by ``price_list_type``; whether it may order is decided
by the credit check.
CustomerType.title: CustomerType

CustomerUpdate.description:
Partial update.

``code`` is not updatable: it is quoted on orders, invoices and customer
statements that have already left the building, so renaming it in place
would make that history ambiguous. Retire the account and create the
replacement instead.

``is_blocked`` is absent as well - a credit hold is a state change with a
mandatory reason, and it goes through the block/unblock endpoints so it
cannot be flipped as a side effect of an unrelated edit.
CustomerUpdate.title: CustomerUpdate

DashboardRead.description:
The management tile set (master rules section 25).

Assembled from summary tables and indexed counts in one round trip and
cached briefly. Every figure here is a *headline*: the tile links to the
report that can be trusted for a decision, and none of these numbers is used
to promise stock (section 34).
DashboardRead.title: DashboardRead

DecideRequest.description:
The verdict, and the full disposition of the lot.

The five quantities must add up to ``inspected_quantity``. Stating the
disposition in full is what makes the stock consequence total: every piece
either leaves QC hold for a named pool or is explicitly left on it.
DecideRequest.title: DecideRequest

DecisionRequest.description: Approval or rejection note, recorded on the document and in the audit log.
DecisionRequest.title: DecisionRequest

DecisionResponse.description: What the decision did, including the stock it moved.
DecisionResponse.title: DecisionResponse

DelayedDispatchRow.description: A consignment past its promised date with no delivery recorded.
DelayedDispatchRow.title: DelayedDispatchRow

DeliveryConfirmation.description: Confirm the receiver has the goods.
DeliveryConfirmation.title: DeliveryConfirmation

DemandSummaryRow.description: Open demand for one item, aggregated across every open order.
DemandSummaryRow.title: DemandSummaryRow

DemandType.description:
What kind of document is asking for the stock.

A closed vocabulary, and deliberately *not* a foreign key: the demand lives
in six different tables and a polymorphic FK is not expressible in SQL. The
pair ``(demand_type, demand_id)`` is the reference, and the index on it is
what makes "release everything this cancelled order was holding" one query.
DemandType.title: DemandType

DispatchCreate.description:
Raise a consignment in ``NOT_DISPATCHED``.

Nothing moves: this is the loading plan. Stock leaves only when
``POST /{id}/dispatch`` runs.
DispatchCreate.title: DispatchCreate

DispatchDetail.description: One consignment with everything captured about it.
DispatchDetail.title: DispatchDetail

DispatchHandoverRequest.description: Claim a packed order for a dispatch.
DispatchHandoverRequest.title: DispatchHandoverRequest

DispatchLineIn.description:
One item to load onto the consignment.

``sales_order_line_id`` is optional even on a dispatch raised against a sales
order: a shipment often carries something the customer did not order on that
line - a replacement part, a sample - and forcing a link would either block
it or invent a demand row for it.
DispatchLineIn.title: DispatchLineIn

DispatchRequest.description: Send the consignment: consume the reservations and post the movements.
DispatchRequest.title: DispatchRequest

DispatchResult.description:
What sending a consignment actually did.

Returned rather than a bare 200 because the caller's next question is always
"did the sales order close, and what did it post?" - and answering it here
saves the UI three follow-up reads.
DispatchResult.title: DispatchResult

DispatchStatus.description:
Lifecycle of a consignment (database.md section 7).

The tail of this list - ``QC_PENDING`` onwards - describes what happens to
the consignment *at the far end*: the receiver inspects it and books it in.
Those statuses are reported to us (a customer's acknowledgement, a vendor
portal, a courier feed) rather than performed by us, which is why every one
of them is reached by recording a tracking event.
DispatchStatus.title: DispatchStatus

DispatchSummary.description:
List row. Deliberately narrower than the detail - a list of fifty
consignments does not need every transport field.
DispatchSummary.title: DispatchSummary

DispatchType.description:
What kind of consignment this is.

Not a cosmetic label: it decides which counterparty column is mandatory and
whether a sales order may be attached at all (see the CHECK constraints).
DispatchType.title: DispatchType

DispatchUpdate.description:
Amend a consignment that has not left yet.

``dispatch_type``, ``customer_id``, ``vendor_id`` and ``sales_order_id`` are
absent on purpose: sending different goods to a different party is a
different consignment, not an edit of this one, and changing them after the
lines were validated against them would leave the document self-inconsistent.
DispatchUpdate.title: DispatchUpdate

DocumentCategory.description:
What the file is for, and therefore where it is stored.

A classification, not a permission: nothing reads this to decide whether a
caller may see the file - that is what the tenant filter and the
``document.*`` permissions do. It selects the storage sub-tree and drives the
default retention applied in :mod:`src.modules.documents.service`.
DocumentCategory.title: DocumentCategory

DocumentRead.description:
Document metadata as returned to a client.

``storage_key`` is absent on purpose - see the module docstring.
DocumentRead.title: DocumentRead

DuplicateCandidateRead.description: An existing open order that the proposed one may be duplicating.
DuplicateCandidateRead.title: DuplicateCandidateRead

DuplicateCheckRequest.description: Ask what an order would collide with, before raising it.
DuplicateCheckRequest.title: DuplicateCheckRequest

EffectivePermissions.description:
The resolved authority of one user, with its provenance.

The breakdown matters as much as the total: "why can this person approve
payments?" is the question an access review actually asks, and a flat list
cannot answer it.
EffectivePermissions.title: EffectivePermissions

ErrorResponse.description: Documented error shape - referenced by every route's responses map.
ErrorResponse.title: ErrorResponse

FinancialYearCreate.description:
Payload for opening a financial year.

``is_closed`` is absent by design: a year is closed through
``POST /financial-years/{id}/close``, which validates the transition and
audits it. Accepting it here would let a create bypass both.
FinancialYearCreate.title: FinancialYearCreate

FinancialYearUpdate.description:
Partial update.

Dates are updatable while the year is open because the first period of a new
deployment is routinely entered before the exact cut-off is agreed. Once the
year is closed the service refuses every edit - that is what closing means.
FinancialYearUpdate.title: FinancialYearUpdate

FreightPaidBy.description:
Who bears the freight on this consignment.

``CONSIGNOR`` is us, the sender; ``CONSIGNEE`` is the receiver. Captured per
consignment rather than inferred from the customer's standing terms: the
terms are a default, this is what was actually agreed for this lorry, and it
decides whether the freight amount is recoverable.
FreightPaidBy.title: FreightPaidBy

GoodsReceiptPostResult.description: What posting a receipt did: stock moved, order advanced, QC raised.
GoodsReceiptPostResult.title: GoodsReceiptPostResult

GoodsReceiptStatus.description:
Lifecycle of a goods receipt.

``POSTED`` is terminal on purpose. Posting writes the inventory ledger, and
an append-only ledger is corrected by an offsetting entry - a purchase
return - never by retracting the document that created it (database.md
section 4.2).
GoodsReceiptStatus.title: GoodsReceiptStatus

GstRateRow.description: One HSN and rate slab within the period.
GstRateRow.title: GstRateRow

GstSection.description: One side of the return: output tax, or input tax.
GstSection.title: GstSection

GstSummary.description: Output tax from sales, input tax from purchases, and the net position.
GstSummary.title: GstSummary

InTransitRequest.description: Report that the consignment is moving, with where it was last seen.
InTransitRequest.title: InTransitRequest

InspectionCreate.description:
Raise an inspection by hand.

Used by a supervisor pulling a lot off the shelf for a final check. The
inspections raised automatically by a goods receipt, a job work return or an
assembly completion come through ``service.create_incoming_inspection`` and
``service.create_in_process_inspection`` instead, and carry the reference of
the document that triggered them.
InspectionCreate.title: InspectionCreate

InspectionResult.description:
The verdict on the goods.

``PENDING`` until a decision is taken. The other five each have exactly one
stock consequence, applied by ``service.decide_inspection``:

``ACCEPTED``  released from QC hold into the available pool.
``REWORK``    stays on QC hold, flagged for rework, re-decided afterwards.
``REJECTED``  moved to the damaged pool: present and counted, promisable to
              nobody, and awaiting a return or a replacement.
``HOLD``      stays on QC hold, undecided, waiting for someone with more
              authority or more information.
``SCRAP``     written off to the scrap pool. It never comes back.
InspectionResult.title: InspectionResult

InspectionStatus.description:
Lifecycle of the inspection document (database.md section 7).

The five decision states duplicate :class:`InspectionResult` on purpose:
``status`` answers "what is left to do with this document", ``result``
answers "what did we conclude about the goods". A check constraint keeps the
two consistent. ``HOLD`` and ``REWORK`` are deliberately not terminal - stock
parked in either still sits in the QC hold pool and has to be re-decided
before it can leave, and a status graph that let it stay there forever would
be modelling the bug rather than the process.
InspectionStatus.title: InspectionStatus

InventoryValuationPage.description:
A page of valuation rows with the totals for the whole filtered set.

The totals sit beside the rows rather than in a second endpoint because a
valuation is meaningless without them - a page showing ten positions out of
four thousand needs to say what the four thousand are worth. The page itself
is still server-bounded and carries its own pagination block.
InventoryValuationPage.title: InventoryValuationPage

InventoryValuationRow.description:
On-hand stock at one item and warehouse, valued FIFO.

``value`` is ``sum(stock_value)`` across the position's balance rows: each
position's open FIFO cost layers, added up and rounded once at the four
places that column stores. ``recorded_value`` is the same total recomputed
straight from the layer rows, so a balance that has drifted from the layers
behind it shows as a difference instead of being reported as fact.
InventoryValuationRow.title: InventoryValuationRow

InvoiceApproval.description:
Approve an invoice, optionally overriding a match variance.

``override_reason`` is what makes an out-of-tolerance approval auditable.
Approval requires ``vendor_invoice.approve``, so supplying it is itself the
exercise of that authority (master rules section 42).
InvoiceApproval.title: InvoiceApproval

IssueLineIn.description:
Send less of one line than the order asked for.

Omitting a line issues its full ``quantity_to_issue``, which is the normal
case. An explicit quantity exists for the reality of a vendor who can only
take half the consignment this week.
IssueLineIn.title: IssueLineIn

IssueRequest.description:
Send the material out under a delivery challan.

The challan fields are on this payload rather than on the order because they
describe the journey, not the instruction: the vehicle and the transporter
are only known on the morning the goods actually leave.
IssueRequest.title: IssueRequest

IssueResult.description: What issuing actually did, so the caller does not have to guess.
IssueResult.title: IssueResult

ItemAttributeType.description:
Which physical attribute a permitted value belongs to.

The *kinds* are fixed in code because each one is a column on ``items`` and
``item_variants``; a fourth kind is a schema change either way. The *values*
are the client's, which is the entire point of the table below - so nothing
anywhere may branch on an ``ItemAttribute.code``.
ItemAttributeType.title: ItemAttributeType

ItemAttributeUpdate.description:
``None`` means "leave alone" on every field.

``attribute`` is absent on purpose: moving a value from FINISH to COLOUR
would silently retarget every item that references it, and the two are
unique per kind, so the move could also collide. Retire it and make a new
one instead.
ItemAttributeUpdate.title: ItemAttributeUpdate

ItemGroup.description:
Reporting classification only.

Master rules section 1: no business rule may branch on this value to decide
whether an operation is allowed. It drives reports, default capability flags
at creation time, and nothing else.
ItemGroup.title: ItemGroup

ItemQualityHistory.description: Rejection rate for one item over a window, and how it moved.
ItemQualityHistory.title: ItemQualityHistory

ItemStatusChange.description:
Activate/deactivate. The reason is mandatory - section 83 applies to
master data lifecycle changes too, and "who turned this item off and why"
is the first question asked when an order line stops validating.
ItemStatusChange.title: ItemStatusChange

ItemUpdate.description: Every field optional; only what is present is written.
ItemUpdate.title: ItemUpdate

JobWorkOrderCreate.description: Raise a draft job work order.
JobWorkOrderCreate.title: JobWorkOrderCreate

JobWorkOrderDetail.description:
Header plus its line set.

Not paginated, by deliberate exception to section 31: the set is bounded by
``MAX_LINES_PER_ORDER`` at write time and a challan is only meaningful whole.
JobWorkOrderDetail.title: JobWorkOrderDetail

JobWorkOrderLineCreate.description:
One material to send out and the processed item expected back.

``expected_output_item_id`` may be omitted when the process does not change
what the thing is - polishing a handle returns a handle - in which case the
input item is used. It is a separate field rather than an assumption because
for PVD, coating and machining the output genuinely is a different code with
a different cost.
JobWorkOrderLineCreate.title: JobWorkOrderLineCreate

JobWorkOrderStatus.description:
Lifecycle of a job work order (database.md section 7).

``CANCELLED`` is reachable only before the material has left the premises.
Once stock is in the job-work pool at a vendor, the order is the only record
of where it went: cancelling would orphan a quantity that is still on the
company's books with nothing to explain it. An order whose material never
comes back is closed after a final receipt writes the shortfall off as
scrap, so the loss is stated rather than implied.
JobWorkOrderStatus.title: JobWorkOrderStatus

JobWorkOrderUpdate.description:
Amend a draft.

Only a DRAFT is editable: past approval the order has hard stock
reservations against it and, from ISSUED, material at a vendor. ``vendor_id``
is absent on purpose - sending the same order to a different processor is a
different order, not an edit, and the challan would name the wrong party.
JobWorkOrderUpdate.title: JobWorkOrderUpdate

JobWorkProcess.description:
What the vendor does to the material.

A classification of the service bought, in the vocabulary master rules
section 20 names. No rule reads it to decide whether an operation is legal -
that is what the item's ``can_job_work`` capability flag is for (database.md
section 3). It drives the vendor picker, the rate card and the process-wise
spend report.
JobWorkProcess.title: JobWorkProcess

JobWorkSourceType.description:
What demand this order was raised to cover.

Read the way procurement reads its own source pair: two orders naming the
same source are covering the same shortage twice.
JobWorkSourceType.title: JobWorkSourceType

LeadTimeRead.description: What MRP asks for: how long making this quantity takes, in whole days.
LeadTimeRead.title: LeadTimeRead

LedgerAccountCreate.description:
Open an account in the chart.

``is_system`` and ``system_code`` are absent on purpose: the accounts the
automatic postings depend on are provisioned by the module itself, and a
client that could claim ``system_code = 'ACCOUNTS_PAYABLE'`` could redirect
every payables posting in the company.
LedgerAccountCreate.title: LedgerAccountCreate

LedgerAccountType.description: The five account classes, which fix the sign of a normal balance.
LedgerAccountType.title: LedgerAccountType

LedgerAccountUpdate.description:
Amend an account. ``account_type`` is not amendable.

Re-typing an account with postings in it would silently restate every report
that has ever been run: the same rows would move from expenses to assets. A
mis-typed account is retired and replaced.
LedgerAccountUpdate.title: LedgerAccountUpdate

LedgerEntryRead.description: One ledger row as the API reports it.
LedgerEntryRead.title: LedgerEntryRead

LedgerStatement.description: A party statement: opening balance, the movements, closing balance.
LedgerStatement.title: LedgerStatement

LedgerStatementRow.description:
One posting on a party statement, with the balance after it.

``running_balance`` is computed by the database with a window function over
the whole filtered set and is therefore correct on every page - a Python
accumulator would only be correct on page one (see the repository).
LedgerStatementRow.title: LedgerStatementRow

LineAllocationRead.description:
What one line got, and what it is still short of.

``shortfall`` is the number MRP has to cover. It is reported per line on the
confirm response so the salesperson sees it immediately rather than
discovering it when the picking list comes up short.
LineAllocationRead.title: LineAllocationRead

MachineCreate.description:
Payload for a new machine.

Neither ``status`` nor ``is_active`` is accepted. A new machine starts
``AVAILABLE`` and active; availability moves through the machine state
machine afterwards, and ``is_active`` is cleared only by retiring it. Letting
a create set either one would make it possible to file a machine that is
simultaneously available and inactive.
MachineCreate.title: MachineCreate

MachineStatus.description:
Availability of one machine.

``RETIRED`` is terminal: a scrapped machine is kept because historical
production entries name it, but it can never come back into a plan.
MachineStatus.title: MachineStatus

MachineStatusChange.description: Move a machine to another availability state.
MachineStatusChange.title: MachineStatusChange

MachineUpdate.description:
Partial update.

``status`` is absent by design: availability moves through the machine state
machine on its own endpoint, so every change carries a reason and an audit
row rather than arriving as one field of a bulk edit.
MachineUpdate.title: MachineUpdate

ManualDemandIn.description:
Demand a planner adds on top of the order book.

A forecast line, a spares top-up, an internal build. It carries no source
document, which is why ``mrp_demands`` allows a null ``source_id`` only for
``MANUAL``.
ManualDemandIn.title: ManualDemandIn

MarkReadResult.description: Outcome of a bulk read acknowledgement.
MarkReadResult.title: MarkReadResult

MatchLineVariance.description:
What one invoice line agreed and disagreed with.

Both variances are reported as a signed money amount *and* as a proportion,
because the tolerance is proportional but the conversation with the vendor
is about rupees.
MatchLineVariance.title: MatchLineVariance

MatchResult.description:
The outcome of matching one vendor invoice against its order and receipt.

``matched`` is the single question approval asks. Everything else exists so
a human can see *why* the answer is no.
MatchResult.title: MatchResult

MatchStatus.description: Outcome of the last three-way match run against an invoice.
MatchStatus.title: MatchStatus

MaterialIssueCreate.description: A draft issue or return. Nothing moves until it is posted.
MaterialIssueCreate.title: MaterialIssueCreate

MaterialIssueStatus.description:
``POSTED`` is terminal on purpose.

Once stock has moved, the document is history. A mistake is corrected with a
return document that posts the offsetting movement, never by editing the
issue - the same rule the inventory ledger itself follows.
MaterialIssueStatus.title: MaterialIssueStatus

MaterialIssueType.description:
Direction of the movement the document posts.

``ISSUE`` posts ``MATERIAL_ISSUE`` out of the store; ``RETURN`` posts
``MATERIAL_RETURN`` back into it.
MaterialIssueType.title: MaterialIssueType

MeResponse.description: Who the caller is and exactly what they may do, resolved this request.
MeResponse.title: MeResponse

MeasurementIn.description:
One reading against one template parameter.

Exactly one value is supplied, and which one is decided by the parameter's
type - the service checks the pair, because a numeric reading typed into the
text field would be compared as a string and "10" would come out below "9".
MeasurementIn.title: MeasurementIn

MfaChallengeResponse.description: Password stage succeeded; no session exists until TOTP verification.
MfaChallengeResponse.title: MfaChallengeResponse

MrpDemandRead.description: One demand line as the run captured it.
MrpDemandRead.title: MrpDemandRead

MrpDemandSource.description:
Where one demand line came from.

Only two, deliberately. Forecast and safety-stock replenishment are separate
planning inputs that master rules section 14 does not describe, and inventing
them here would let a plan claim a provenance the system cannot substantiate.
MrpDemandSource.title: MrpDemandSource

MrpRequirementRead.description:
One merged requirement, with every figure that went into it.

The netting inputs are all present on purpose: "we are 40 short" cannot be
reviewed, and "gross 200 = 100 direct + 100 from bills of materials, 60 free
of 160 on hand, 100 already on order, so 40 short" can.

That includes the supply the run deliberately did *not* net. The two
quantities and the two dates beside them are the per-row form of the run's
``late_supply_item_count`` and its "arrives AFTER it is needed" warning: an
order exists, it lands on this date, and the shortage beside it stands
anyway. A client that had only the warning would have to parse an English
sentence to render a row, which is fragile and untranslatable.

Each quantity carries **its own INTERVAL**, not a single date. A late
quantity is a SUM over that feed's late tranches, so one date beside it is a
whole fact only when the feed had one tranche; with several, the earliest
date understates how late the bulk is, which reads as "nearly here". So
``late_incoming_quantity`` opens at ``first_late_incoming_date`` and is
complete by ``last_late_incoming_date``, and ``late_in_production_quantity``
likewise. Render the interval - "the first of 5010 on 2026-07-30, all of it
by 2026-12-15" - never the quantity against one end of it. The two feeds are
independent schedules and pairing either quantity with the other's dates is
a false statement. The
single ``first_late_supply_date`` is the earlier of the two and answers only
"how soon does anything land at all" - it used to be the only date on the
row, which made "5000 on order" beside a 0.0001 job's date read as five
thousand arriving the next day.

``late_supply_quantity`` is the sum of the two, computed here so a client
never adds two decimal strings in JavaScript and gets a float back. There is
deliberately no summed-quantity-plus-summary-date pair: that combination is
the misreading above, written down.

late_supply_quantity.description: Everything the phasing excluded for this row, from either source.
late_supply_quantity.title: Late Supply Quantity

MrpRequirementRead.title: MrpRequirementRead

MrpRunMode.description:
How the run was executed.

Recorded rather than inferred from ``celery_task_id``: a run dispatched to a
worker that never started still needs to say it was meant to be asynchronous.
MrpRunMode.title: MrpRunMode

MrpRunRead.description:
One run with everything it was given and everything it produced.

``warnings`` is not decoration. It carries the netting stages the run could
not perform - a missing procurement module, a make item with no bill of
materials - and a planner reading suggestions without reading these would be
trusting numbers the engine already knows are an upper bound.

It also carries the supply the run deliberately did *not* count: an order or
a job inside the horizon that arrives after the demand needs it. That is a
shortage a buyer will otherwise query - "we have a purchase order for these"
- so the plan names each feed's quantity with the date that feed lands,
rather than leaving the two facts unconnected or pairing one date with a
quantity from the other feed. ``result_summary["late_supply_item_count"]``
is the same statement as a number, and :class:`MrpRequirementRead` carries
the quantities and a date per feed, which is where a client should read them
from: this text is prose, written in one language, for a human.

``result_summary["demand_dates_settled"]`` reports the property those
figures rest on: that every item's needed-by date was final before any
supply was phased against it. It is ``True`` on any plan a planner will see;
``False`` means a structure so deep the dates were still moving, which is
also named in a warning, and the component demand underneath those items may
be understated.
MrpRunRead.title: MrpRunRead

MrpRunRequest.description:
Start a planning run.

Nothing here says how the run should execute. That is the service's decision,
taken from the demand-line count against
``settings.mrp_sync_threshold_demand_lines`` (database.md section 6): a
client cannot ask for a four-minute calculation to be held open on an HTTP
connection.
MrpRunRequest.title: MrpRunRequest

MrpRunStatus.description:
Lifecycle of one planning run (database.md section 6).

``QUEUED`` exists only for runs handed to Celery. A run executed inline goes
straight to ``RUNNING``, so "queued" always means "a worker has not picked
this up yet" rather than "something is happening somewhere".
MrpRunStatus.title: MrpRunStatus

MrpRunSummary.description: One row of the run list.
MrpRunSummary.title: MrpRunSummary

MrpSuggestionRead.description: One suggestion and what has happened to it.
MrpSuggestionRead.title: MrpSuggestionRead

MrpSuggestionStatus.description:
Whether a suggestion has been acted on.

``IGNORED`` is a decision, not a deletion: the row stays so the next run's
output can be compared against what a planner already rejected.
MrpSuggestionStatus.title: MrpSuggestionStatus

MrpSuggestionType.description:
What the planner is being told to do about a shortage.

``TRANSFER`` is part of the contract vocabulary (database.md section 6) but
is not produced by this engine: proposing a transfer means comparing free
stock across warehouses the run was explicitly told not to plan against, and
that warehouse-balancing pass is not part of the section 14 flow. The value
exists so a future pass, or a planner editing a suggestion, can use it.
MrpSuggestionType.title: MrpSuggestionType

NotificationPreferenceRead.description:
Effective preference for one type.

Returned for *every* :class:`NotificationType`, including the ones with no
stored row - a preferences screen has to render the whole matrix, and asking
the client to know the defaults would let the two drift apart.
NotificationPreferenceRead.title: NotificationPreferenceRead

NotificationPreferenceUpdate.description: One checkbox row of the preferences matrix.
NotificationPreferenceUpdate.title: NotificationPreferenceUpdate

NotificationRead.description: One row of the bell feed.
NotificationRead.title: NotificationRead

NotificationSeverity.description:
How loudly the UI should present the notification.

A presentation and escalation classification, never an authorisation one.
``CRITICAL`` additionally overrides an in-app opt-out - see
``SEVERITIES_IGNORING_PREFERENCES`` in the service.
NotificationSeverity.title: NotificationSeverity

NotificationType.description:
The closed vocabulary of things the system notifies about.

Closed rather than free text because it is the key of
``notification_preferences``: a user mutes a *type*, so a caller inventing an
ad-hoc string would produce alerts nobody can ever turn off, and a
preferences screen that cannot enumerate its own rows. Adding a member is a
normal code change - it appears in the preferences endpoint automatically and
inherits the defaults in :mod:`src.modules.notifications.service`.
NotificationType.title: NotificationType

OffsetPagination.description:
Page/limit metadata.

``total`` is optional on purpose: counting a large filtered set costs a
second full scan, so list endpoints over very large tables may omit it
rather than pay for a number nobody reads (section 31).
OffsetPagination.title: OffsetPagination

OperationCostRead.description: One step's contribution to the routing cost, at a stated quantity.
OperationCostRead.title: OperationCostRead

OrderAllocationRead.description: Per-line reserved versus shortfall for one order.
OrderAllocationRead.title: OrderAllocationRead

OutstandingRow.description: One open vendor invoice, aged against the report date.
OutstandingRow.title: OutstandingRow

PackingCompletionResult.description: What completion froze, so the caller does not have to re-read to find out.
PackingCompletionResult.title: PackingCompletionResult

PackingHandoverRequest.description: Claim a completed assembly for a packing order.
PackingHandoverRequest.title: PackingHandoverRequest

PackingMaterialRow.description:
An item offered as packing material on the carton form.

A pick-list, not a rule: ``item_group`` is a reporting and default-behaviour
classification (database.md section 3), so it decides what is *suggested*
here and never what is *permitted* when a carton is sealed.
PackingMaterialRow.title: PackingMaterialRow

PackingOrderDetail.description:
Header plus its line set.

Lines are not paginated, by deliberate exception to section 31: the set is
bounded by ``MAX_LINES_PER_ORDER`` at write time and a packing list is only
meaningful whole.
PackingOrderDetail.title: PackingOrderDetail

PackingOrderLineIn.description:
One item to be boxed.

``sales_order_line_id`` is optional even on an order raised against a sales
order: a shipment often includes something the customer did not order on
that line - a replacement part, a sample - and forcing a link would either
block it or invent a demand row for it.
PackingOrderLineIn.title: PackingOrderLineIn

PackingOrderStatus.description:
Lifecycle of a packing order (master rules section 22).

``PACKED`` means the goods are boxed, sealed and weighed - not that they have
left. ``HANDED_OVER`` is the moment a dispatch takes responsibility for them,
and it is the dispatch module that sets it. ``CANCELLED`` is reachable only
before ``PACKED``: past that, cartons are sealed and packing material has
been consumed, so the way out is to close the order rather than to claim it
never happened.
PackingOrderStatus.title: PackingOrderStatus

PackingOrderUpdate.description:
Amend a draft.

Only a DRAFT is editable: from IN_PROGRESS the bench has boxes open against
these lines, and from PACKED the material has been consumed. ``customer_id``
and ``sales_order_id`` are absent on purpose - shipping to a different
customer is a different order, not an edit of this one.
PackingOrderUpdate.title: PackingOrderUpdate

ParameterEvaluationRead.description:
What the recorded measurements imply, before anybody decides anything.

Returned by the record-results endpoint so the inspector sees the
consequence of what they just typed - in particular that a critical failure
has already settled the verdict.
ParameterEvaluationRead.title: ParameterEvaluationRead

ParameterType.description:
What kind of value a parameter records, and therefore how it is judged.

The type decides which ``measured_value_*`` column carries the reading and
which specification columns are meaningful: a tolerance band belongs to a
NUMERIC parameter and nothing else, and an ``allowed_values`` list belongs to
a SELECT. Storing a number as text would make every range check a string
comparison, which is how "10" comes out smaller than "9".
ParameterType.title: ParameterType

PartyType.description: Who a ledger entry or a payment is against.
PartyType.title: PartyType

PasswordResetRequest.description:
Administrator-triggered password reset.

``new_password`` is optional. Omitting it makes the server generate a
single-use temporary password and return it once, which is the safer
default: an administrator who invents passwords tends to reuse the same one
for every account they touch.
PasswordResetRequest.title: PasswordResetRequest

PasswordResetResult.description:
Outcome of a reset.

``temporary_password`` is populated only when the server generated one, is
returned exactly once, and is never stored in plaintext nor written to the
audit log (``src.modules.audit.service`` strips it in any case).
PasswordResetResult.title: PasswordResetResult

PaymentCreate.description:
Record a payment or receipt in DRAFT. Nothing posts until approval.

Allocations are deliberately absent: money can only settle an invoice once
it has actually moved, so a draft has nothing to allocate. Settlement is
``POST /payments/{id}/allocate`` on an approved payment.
PaymentCreate.title: PaymentCreate

PaymentStatus.description:
Lifecycle of a payment or receipt.

Money moves at APPROVED - that is where the journal is posted and where the
party's outstanding balance changes. Allocation afterwards decides *which
invoices* it settled, and cannot change the amount that left the bank.
PaymentStatus.title: PaymentStatus

PaymentUpdate.description: Amend a payment that has not been approved.
PaymentUpdate.title: PaymentUpdate

PendingApproval.description: One document waiting on the caller's decision.
PendingApproval.title: PendingApproval

PendingAtVendorRow.description:
Company material currently at one vendor, for one item.

Every quantity here is stock the company still owns and still values; it is
simply not available to promise. The ageing is measured from the despatch,
which is why an order that has been open for six months shows up even if its
expected return date was quietly pushed back.
PendingAtVendorRow.title: PendingAtVendorRow

PermissionCatalogue.description:
The complete registry, grouped for the permission-matrix UI.

Not paginated, deliberately: this is a compiled-in vocabulary of a fixed
size, not a query over tenant data that can grow. Paginating it would force
the matrix screen to make several round trips to render one fixed table.
PermissionCatalogue.title: PermissionCatalogue

PermissionEntry.description: One cell of the permission matrix.
PermissionEntry.title: PermissionEntry

PermissionGroup.description: One section of the matrix, in the order the registry declares it.
PermissionGroup.title: PermissionGroup

PhysicalCountCreate.description: Creates the sheet and snapshots system quantities for its scope.
PhysicalCountCreate.title: PhysicalCountCreate

PreferencesUpdateRequest.description:
The rows the user changed.

Partial by design: sending only the touched rows keeps an old client from
silently resetting a type it does not know about yet.

Turning every channel off for a type is allowed - it is the user's own inbox
- and is not rejected here. CRITICAL alerts still reach the bell regardless;
that override lives in the service, next to the constant that names it.
PreferencesUpdateRequest.title: PreferencesUpdateRequest

PriceType.description: Which commercial channel a price list row applies to.
PriceType.title: PriceType

ProductionCostRead.description:
Actual cost of one job.

Recomputed live for an open order and read back from the stored columns
once the order is closed - a closed job's cost must not move when a
work-centre rate is revised.
ProductionCostRead.title: ProductionCostRead

ProductionOrderCreate.description: Raise a DRAFT order. Nothing is planned against stock yet.
ProductionOrderCreate.title: ProductionOrderCreate

ProductionOrderDetail.description:
The order with its operations.

Work orders are included inline rather than paginated because a routing is
bounded at write time (``MAX_OPERATIONS_PER_ROUTING`` in the routing module)
and a traveller is only meaningful whole. Components are *not* included:
a multi-level explosion is not bounded that way, so they have their own
paginated endpoint.
ProductionOrderDetail.title: ProductionOrderDetail

ProductionOrderStatus.description:
Database contract section 7, verbatim.

``DRAFT -> APPROVED -> RELEASED -> MATERIAL_ISSUED -> IN_PROCESS ->
COMPLETED -> CLOSED``, with ``CANCELLED`` reachable only before the job is
physically under way.
ProductionOrderStatus.title: ProductionOrderStatus

ProductionOrderSummary.description: List row. Deliberately narrower than the detail.
ProductionOrderSummary.title: ProductionOrderSummary

ProductionOrderUpdate.description: Partial update of a draft. Only the keys actually sent are applied.
ProductionOrderUpdate.title: ProductionOrderUpdate

ProductionSourceType.description:
Where the demand for this order came from.

Not a foreign key: the source is an MRP suggestion, a sales order or nothing
at all, and a polymorphic FK is not expressible in SQL. The pair
``(source_type, source_id)`` is the reference and is indexed as one.
ProductionSourceType.title: ProductionSourceType

ProductionType.description: How the item is normally obtained. Drives MRP suggestion type.
ProductionType.title: ProductionType

PurchaseOrderLineStatus.description:
Fulfilment state of one order line.

Derived from the quantities by ``service.po_line_status_for`` rather than
set independently, so a line can never claim RECEIVED while its received
quantity is short.
PurchaseOrderLineStatus.title: PurchaseOrderLineStatus

PurchaseOrderStatus.description:
Lifecycle of a purchase order (database.md section 7).

``CANCELLED`` is reachable only before anything has been received. Once
stock has physically moved against the order, cancelling it would leave the
inventory ledger describing a receipt against a document claiming never to
have existed; a partially received order is short-closed instead.
PurchaseOrderStatus.title: PurchaseOrderStatus

PurchaseOrderTracking.description: The dispatch-tracking view of one inbound order.
PurchaseOrderTracking.title: PurchaseOrderTracking

PurchaseOrderVendorAssignee.description:
A vendor user an order may be sent to - the Send dialog's picker row.

Served by procurement because the buyer choosing the assignee holds
``purchase_order.send``, not ``user.view``.
PurchaseOrderVendorAssignee.title: PurchaseOrderVendorAssignee

PurchaseSourceType.description:
Where a procurement document's demand came from.

Read by the duplicate matcher: two orders that name the same source demand
are covering the same shortage twice, which is the strongest duplicate
signal there is (master rules section 16).
PurchaseSourceType.title: PurchaseSourceType

QcStage.description:
Where in the flow the inspection happens.

A classification of *when*, not of what is permitted: no rule reads this to
decide whether an operation is legal. It selects the template, groups the
pending queue by the team that works it, and is the axis the quality reports
slice on.
QcStage.title: QcStage

QcVerdictItem.description: The verdict on one held output item.
QcVerdictItem.title: QcVerdictItem

QualityPeriodRow.description: One month of an item's quality history.
QualityPeriodRow.title: QualityPeriodRow

QuotationComparison.description: Side-by-side comparison of every quotation received for one RFQ.
QuotationComparison.title: QuotationComparison

QuotationDecisionRequest.description:
Select or reject one quotation.

The reason is required even when following the recommendation: the buyer's
judgement is the record, and the comparison's score is only its input.
QuotationDecisionRequest.title: QuotationDecisionRequest

QuotationStatus.description: Lifecycle of one vendor's response to an RFQ.
QuotationStatus.title: QuotationStatus

QuotationUpdate.description: A revised offer from the same vendor against the same RFQ.
QuotationUpdate.title: QuotationUpdate

RateBasis.description:
How the vendor's charge is computed.

``PER_PIECE`` and ``PER_KG`` both multiply the rate by a quantity in the
line's own unit of measure - the difference is which unit the rate card was
agreed in, and it is recorded so an invoice can be checked against the
order. ``LOT`` is a flat charge for the consignment however much comes back,
which is why it is accrued once rather than per unit.
RateBasis.title: RateBasis

ReadyForDispatchRow.description:
A packed order no dispatch has claimed yet.

This is the contract the ``dispatch`` module consumes. ``carton_count`` is
counted from the carton rows rather than read from ``total_cartons`` so the
feed cannot advertise a number the boxes disagree with.
ReadyForDispatchRow.title: ReadyForDispatchRow

ReadyForPackingRow.description:
A completed assembly whose output is packable.

``available_quantity`` is read from ``inventory_balances`` at the output
position and is never cached (section 34): it is the number that decides
whether a packing order can actually be filled.
ReadyForPackingRow.title: ReadyForPackingRow

ReallocationCandidateRead.description:
One reservation a reallocation could take from, and why it ranked here.

``reasons`` is not decoration. The approver is being asked to disappoint a
demand, and a ranked list with no explanation is a list nobody trusts.
ReallocationCandidateRead.title: ReallocationCandidateRead

ReallocationDecision.description: Approve or reject a request. The note is what the requester will read.
ReallocationDecision.title: ReallocationDecision

ReallocationRequestCreate.description:
Ask for stock currently promised elsewhere.

``from_reservation_id`` is optional: leave it out and the engine ranks the
donors and picks the best one, which is the normal path from a shortage
screen. Name one explicitly when a planner has already decided which demand
should give way.
ReallocationRequestCreate.title: ReallocationRequestCreate

ReallocationRequestRead.description: A reallocation request and everything a decision needs.
ReallocationRequestRead.title: ReallocationRequestRead

ReallocationStatus.description:
Lifecycle of a request to move a promise from one demand to another.

``APPROVED`` and ``EXECUTED`` are separate states even though the service
performs both inside one transaction: the approval is the human decision and
the execution is its effect, and an audit that cannot distinguish them
cannot answer "was this signed off before the stock moved?".
ReallocationStatus.title: ReallocationStatus

ReceiptLineIn.description:
What one order line gave back in this lot.

``output_quantity`` and ``rejected_quantity`` are both *output* units;
``returned_unprocessed_quantity`` is *input* material handed back untouched.
They are separate fields because they post to three different places, and a
single "received" number would make it impossible to say which.
ReceiptLineIn.title: ReceiptLineIn

ReceiptLineQcStatus.description:
Incoming-inspection state of one received line.

``PENDING`` is the flag the quality module picks up when it is not present
at posting time: the quantity is already sitting in ``QC_HOLD`` and needs an
inspection raised against it.
ReceiptLineQcStatus.title: ReceiptLineQcStatus

ReceiveRequest.description: Record one lot returning from the vendor.
ReceiveRequest.title: ReceiveRequest

ReconciliationLine.description:
Issued against received, for one order line.

``outstanding_quantity`` is the number that has to equal the line's share of
``inventory_balances.job_work_quantity``. When they disagree, either a
movement was posted outside this module or a receipt was recorded without
one - both are corruption of the traceability the module exists to keep.
ReconciliationLine.title: ReconciliationLine

ReconciliationReport.description:
Issued vs received vs loss for one job work order.

The report a plant manager reads before paying a job worker, and the one an
auditor reads to satisfy themselves that stock sent out was accounted for.
ReconciliationReport.title: ReconciliationReport

RecordResultsRequest.description: Record or correct a set of measurements on an inspection.
RecordResultsRequest.title: RecordResultsRequest

RejectionAction.description:
What happens to output the vendor produced badly.

Three dispositions, each with exactly one posting rule, because "rejected"
on its own does not say where the goods physically are:

``RETURN_TO_STOCK``   the bad pieces came back. They are received into the
                      ``DAMAGED`` pool - present, counted, not promisable -
                      and their share of the input is drawn out of the
                      job-work pool.
``REWORK_AT_VENDOR``  the vendor keeps them and reprocesses them. Nothing
                      moves: the input stays in the job-work pool, the line
                      stays open, and the quantity keeps appearing in
                      ``pending-at-vendor`` with its true ageing. This is
                      what makes rework traceable instead of a note in a
                      comment box.
``SCRAP_AT_VENDOR``   they were destroyed there. The input share moves from
                      the job-work pool to ``SCRAP`` and never comes home.
RejectionAction.title: RejectionAction

ReportColumnRead.description: One column of a report, for a client that renders the grid generically.
ReportColumnRead.title: ReportColumnRead

ReportDescriptorRead.description: What a report is and what it needs - drives the report picker.
ReportDescriptorRead.title: ReportDescriptorRead

ReportJobRead.description: Status and result of a background report (``GET /reports/jobs/{id}``).
ReportJobRead.title: ReportJobRead

ReportJobStatus.description:
Lifecycle of a generated report artefact.

``QUEUED -> FAILED`` is a real edge, not a defensive one: the broker can
refuse the task, and a job left in QUEUED forever would be polled by a client
that never gets an answer.
ReportJobStatus.title: ReportJobStatus

ReportKey.description:
The closed catalogue of reports (master rules section 25).

Closed rather than free text because it is a stored column: it keys the
snapshot lookup, the cache entry and the artefact, so an ad-hoc string would
produce files nothing can ever find again. Adding a member is a normal code
change - a definition in ``service.REPORT_CATALOGUE`` and a route - and the
catalogue asserts at import that every member has exactly one definition.
ReportKey.title: ReportKey

RequisitionBatchConversionRequest.description: The batch form: several approved requisitions converted together.
RequisitionBatchConversionRequest.title: RequisitionBatchConversionRequest

RequisitionConversionGroup.description: One proposed purchase order: one vendor, one category, one warehouse.
RequisitionConversionGroup.title: RequisitionConversionGroup

RequisitionConversionLine.description: One requisition line as it will appear on the proposed order.
RequisitionConversionLine.title: RequisitionConversionLine

RequisitionConversionLineOverride.description: The buyer's correction to how one requisition line is converted.
RequisitionConversionLineOverride.title: RequisitionConversionLineOverride

RequisitionConversionRequest.description:
How to turn approved requisitions into purchase orders.

Every header field applies to every order the conversion raises. Nothing
names a vendor, a category or an assignee per order: those are resolved,
and the per-line overrides are how a buyer changes the resolution.
RequisitionConversionRequest.title: RequisitionConversionRequest

RequisitionConversionUnresolvedLine.description: A line that cannot be converted, and every reason why.
RequisitionConversionUnresolvedLine.title: RequisitionConversionUnresolvedLine

RequisitionListRow.description:
A requisition as the list shows it.

``open_line_count`` is how many of its lines still have quantity to order -
live lines whose ordered quantity is short of the requested one - so the
list can offer "Raise purchase orders" only where there is something left
to raise. Counted for the whole page in one grouped statement.
RequisitionListRow.title: RequisitionListRow

RequisitionPriceSource.description: Where a converted line's unit price came from, strongest source first.
RequisitionPriceSource.title: RequisitionPriceSource

RequisitionStatus.description: Lifecycle of a purchase requisition (master rules section 15).
RequisitionStatus.title: RequisitionStatus

RequisitionUpdate.description:
Partial update of a draft requisition.

``lines`` replaces the whole set when present: a patch language for
individual lines would need its own add/change/remove vocabulary, and the
document is small enough that resending it is honest about what the result
will be.
RequisitionUpdate.title: RequisitionUpdate

RequisitionVendorSource.description: Where a converted line's vendor came from, strongest source first.
RequisitionVendorSource.title: RequisitionVendorSource

ReservationCreate.description: Ask for a quantity of stock to be held for a demand line.
ReservationCreate.title: ReservationCreate

ReservationRead.description: One reservation, with the labels a screen needs to render it.
ReservationRead.title: ReservationRead

ReservationStatus.description:
Lifecycle of one reservation.

``PARTIALLY_CONSUMED`` is a state of its own rather than an inference from
the quantities because a partial issue is the normal case in manufacturing -
a production order draws its components over several days - and the status
index is what keeps the "still holding stock" query cheap.
ReservationStatus.title: ReservationStatus

ReservationType.description:
How firm the promise is.

``HARD`` is a commitment somebody has made to a customer or to a shop floor
that is already tooled up for it; it can only be taken away through an
approved :class:`ReallocationRequest`. ``SOFT`` is a planning placeholder -
MRP's opinion about what a future order will need - and exists precisely so
that a firm order can outrank it.
ReservationType.title: ReservationType

ResolvedPrice.description: What the item actually costs a given channel at a given quantity.
ResolvedPrice.title: ResolvedPrice

RfqStatus.description:
Lifecycle of a request for quotation.

Quotations arriving do not move the RFQ: an RFQ with two of five responses
in is still an open RFQ, and a status that flickered on every vendor reply
would say nothing a buyer could act on.
RfqStatus.title: RfqStatus

RoleAssignment.description:
Replace a user's entire role set.

Replace rather than add/remove: a UI that shows a checklist and posts the
result cannot express "remove this one" as an add, and two administrators
editing the same user concurrently with add/remove deltas silently merge
into a set neither of them chose.

An empty list is legal and means "this account holds no roles"; it keeps
only whatever direct grants it has.
RoleAssignment.title: RoleAssignment

RoleCreate.description:
Payload for creating a role.

``is_system`` is absent: system roles are seeded from
:data:`src.core.permissions.ROLE_PRESETS`. A client-created role that
claimed to be one would be undeletable for a reason nobody could trace.
RoleCreate.title: RoleCreate

RoleDetail.description: Single-role view: the permission matrix and how many people hold it.
RoleDetail.title: RoleDetail

RoleSummary.description:
Role list row.

``permission_count`` rather than the array itself: a permission matrix is a
detail view, and a grid that carried 200 strings per row would be an order
of magnitude larger than the data anyone is reading.
RoleSummary.title: RoleSummary

RoleUpdate.description:
Partial update of a role.

``code`` is not updatable: it appears in seed data, in
:attr:`src.core.deps.Principal.role_codes` and in historical audit rows, so
renaming it in place would make that history ambiguous.

``is_vendor_role`` is not updatable either - flipping it would, in a single
statement, either strip the portal boundary from every holder or make every
holder illegal. Create the role you actually want and reassign.
RoleUpdate.title: RoleUpdate

RoutingCostRead.description: Costed routing for a quantity, with the lead time it implies.
RoutingCostRead.title: RoutingCostRead

RoutingCreate.description: Payload for a new DRAFT routing.
RoutingCreate.title: RoutingCreate

RoutingOperationIn.description: One step on a create or update payload.
RoutingOperationIn.title: RoutingOperationIn

RoutingStatus.description:
Lifecycle of one routing version.

Only ``APPROVED`` routings are visible to planning and production.
``OBSOLETE`` is terminal - a superseded process is retained because the
orders raised against it still reference it.
RoutingStatus.title: RoutingStatus

RoutingUpdate.description:
Partial update of a DRAFT routing.

``operations`` replaces the whole set when present and is left untouched
when absent - a partial merge would need stable client-side ids for rows the
client never saw.
RoutingUpdate.title: RoutingUpdate

SalesOrderCreate.description: Create a DRAFT sales order with its lines.
SalesOrderCreate.title: SalesOrderCreate

SalesOrderLineIn.description: One line on a create or update payload.
SalesOrderLineIn.title: SalesOrderLineIn

SalesOrderLineStatus.description:
Fulfilment state of one order line.

Derived from the quantities rather than set independently - see
``service.line_status_for`` - so a line can never claim ALLOCATED while
``allocated_quantity`` is short of ``quantity``.
SalesOrderLineStatus.title: SalesOrderLineStatus

SalesOrderStatus.description:
Lifecycle of a sales order (database.md section 7).

``CANCELLED`` is reachable only before anything has physically shipped;
after a dispatch the order is closed off through the dispatch and invoice
path instead, because cancelling a document that moved stock would leave the
ledger describing a movement against a document claiming never to have
existed.
SalesOrderStatus.title: SalesOrderStatus

SalesOrderSummary.description:
List row. Deliberately without the lines - a page of 50 orders must not
drag several hundred line rows with it.
SalesOrderSummary.title: SalesOrderSummary

SalesOrderUpdate.description:
Partial update.

Omitting ``lines`` leaves the line set alone. Sending it replaces the set on
a draft, and adjusts quantities on a confirmed order - the service decides,
because the rule depends on the order's status.
SalesOrderUpdate.title: SalesOrderUpdate

SamplingPlan.description:
How much of a delivered lot is actually measured.

``ALL``            every piece. The default when nothing else is configured.
``PERCENTAGE``     a proportion of the lot, rounded up, never below one.
``FIXED_SAMPLE``   a constant number of pieces whatever the lot size.
``AQL``            ISO 2859-1 general inspection level II: the sample grows
                   with the lot but far more slowly than a percentage, which
                   is the entire point of a statistical plan.
SamplingPlan.title: SamplingPlan

SealCartonRequest.description: Close a carton: freeze its contents and issue the box from stock.
SealCartonRequest.title: SealCartonRequest

SealResult.description: A sealed carton and the packing material it cost.
SealResult.title: SealResult

ShipmentUpdate.description: Courier details for the inbound leg (master rules section 23).
ShipmentUpdate.title: ShipmentUpdate

StockState.description:
Which pool a quantity belongs to.

``AVAILABLE`` and ``RETURN`` are the free pool: physically here and usable
(a customer return is ordinary stock until somebody puts it on hold).
``QC_HOLD`` and ``DAMAGED`` are present-but-unusable sub-pools of on-hand.
``IN_TRANSIT``, ``JOB_WORK`` and ``SCRAP`` are company-owned quantities that
are not physically in this position.
StockState.title: StockState

StockTransferUpdate.description: Header edits, allowed only while the transfer is still a draft.
StockTransferUpdate.title: StockTransferUpdate

StorageLocationCreate.description:
Payload for creating a storage location.

``warehouse_id`` comes from the path, not the body - a bin cannot be created
into a warehouse other than the one addressed by the URL.
StorageLocationCreate.title: StorageLocationCreate

StorageLocationType.description: Physical shape of a storage position.
StorageLocationType.title: StorageLocationType

StorageLocationUpdate.description: Partial update of a storage location. ``code`` is immutable, as for warehouses.
StorageLocationUpdate.title: StorageLocationUpdate

SuggestionConversionResult.description:
What conversion actually achieved.

``handled`` is the field that matters and is never inferred from the
suggestion's status: false means no document exists yet and the caller is
holding the only copy of the instruction. Reporting that plainly is the
difference between a seam and a silent gap.
SuggestionConversionResult.title: SuggestionConversionResult

SuggestionConvertRequest.description:
Turn one suggestion into a document.

``target`` may be omitted, in which case it is derived from the suggestion
type. ``quantity`` may be omitted, in which case the suggested quantity is
used; a planner raising a *smaller* order than suggested is knowingly leaving
a shortage, so the value is accepted but the suggestion still records what
was planned.
SuggestionConvertRequest.title: SuggestionConvertRequest

TemplateCreate.description: Create version 1 of an inspection specification.
TemplateCreate.title: TemplateCreate

TemplateParameterIn.description:
One row of a template's check sheet, as submitted.

The type/specification agreement is validated here as well as by the database
check constraints: a tolerance band typed against a BOOLEAN parameter would
otherwise be accepted by the API and then silently ignored by the evaluator,
which is worse than a rejection because the template looks configured.
TemplateParameterIn.title: TemplateParameterIn

TemplateUpdate.description:
Amend a template.

``name``, ``description`` and ``is_active`` are always editable - they change
how the template is presented and whether it is selected, not what it means.
Everything else, including the parameter set, is editable only while the
template has never been applied to an inspection; afterwards the change forks
a new version, so past pass/fail results stay reproducible against the
specification they were judged by.
TemplateUpdate.title: TemplateUpdate

TemplateVersionRequest.description:
Fork a used template into a new revision.

The new version starts from the current one's parameter set unless a
replacement is supplied, so a single tolerance change does not mean retyping
a forty-line check sheet.
TemplateVersionRequest.title: TemplateVersionRequest

TrackingBoardRow.description:
One row of the admin tracking board (master rules section 23).

Every column here comes out of one joined query. ``is_delayed``,
