``qc_pending`` and ``grn_pending`` are computed in SQL rather than in Python
so the board can be filtered and sorted on them without reading the whole
table first.
TrackingBoardRow.title: TrackingBoardRow

TrackingEventIn.description:
Record one reported position or status.

An event whose ``event_status`` differs from the consignment's current status
also moves it, through the state machine - which is why the vocabulary is the
same one. An event repeating the current status is a position update.
TrackingEventIn.title: TrackingEventIn

TrackingEventSource.description:
Where a tracking event came from.

Recorded because the three sources differ in trustworthiness. A ``MANUAL``
event is somebody's typing; a ``COURIER_API`` event is the carrier's own
scan. When they disagree, the source is what lets a human decide which to
believe.
TrackingEventSource.title: TrackingEventSource

TrackingLinkRead.description: A tracking id resolved against a transporter's template.
TrackingLinkRead.title: TrackingLinkRead

TransactionType.description:
The movement vocabulary from master rules section 83.

Every member has a fixed sign (:data:`TRANSACTION_SIGNS`). The sign is a
property of the *type*, never of the caller's arithmetic: a receipt that
arrives with a negative quantity is a mis-keyed document, not a clever way
to express an issue.
TransactionType.title: TransactionType

tracking_url_template.description: HTTPS URL containing the literal {tracking_id} placeholder
tracking_url_template.title: Tracking Url Template

TransporterType.description: Carrier shape. Drives the default tracking behaviour on a dispatch.
TransporterType.title: TransporterType

TransporterUpdate.description: Partial update. ``code`` is immutable, as for vendors.
TransporterUpdate.title: TransporterUpdate

UomCategory.description:
Measurement family. Conversions only exist inside one family.

KG -> NOS is not a unit conversion, it is an item-specific weight, so the
conversion resolver refuses it rather than inventing a factor.
UomCategory.title: UomCategory

UserCreate.description:
Payload for creating an internal staff or vendor-portal account.

``is_superuser`` is deliberately absent - see the ASSUMPTION note in the
service. ``must_change_password`` defaults to True because an administrator
choosing someone else's first password means that password has been typed
into a chat window or read out over a telephone.
UserCreate.title: UserCreate

UserDetail.description: Single-user view, including the roles it holds.
UserDetail.title: UserDetail

UserSummary.description:
List row.

Narrower than the detail model on purpose: a user grid renders none of the
scope arrays or the preferences blob, and loading them would mean selecting
two ARRAY columns and a JSONB column for every row on every page.
UserSummary.title: UserSummary

UserUpdate.description:
Partial update of a user.

Absent on purpose:

* ``is_active`` - activation is a lifecycle change with a mandatory reason
  that also revokes sessions, so it goes through the activate/deactivate
  endpoints rather than being flippable as a side effect of an edit.
* ``role_ids`` - the role set is replaced wholesale through
  ``POST /users/{id}/roles``, which is gated on ``permission.assign`` rather
  than on the much more widely granted ``user.update``.
* ``is_superuser`` - see the service.
UserUpdate.title: UserUpdate

VendorAssigneeReason.description: Why an order was - or was not - handed to a particular vendor user.
VendorAssigneeReason.title: VendorAssigneeReason

VendorCategoryAssign.description: Qualify a vendor for one item category.
VendorCategoryAssign.title: VendorCategoryAssign

VendorChargeRow.description:
One vendor's job work charges for a period.

The contract ``finance`` consumes. Charges accrue on receipt - a vendor is
paid for good pieces delivered - so the period is applied to
``job_work_receipts.receipt_date`` rather than to the order date.
``net_charges`` is what is actually payable: gross processing charges less
the value of company material the vendor lost beyond the agreed allowance.
VendorChargeRow.title: VendorChargeRow

VendorContactCreate.description: A person at the vendor. ``vendor_id`` comes from the path, not the body.
VendorContactCreate.title: VendorContactCreate

VendorContactRole.description:
Portal role of a named contact at the vendor (section 16).

Mirrors the ``VENDOR_*`` role presets in :mod:`src.core.permissions`, so the
contact captured on the master record and the portal login eventually
provisioned for that person describe the same job.
VendorContactRole.title: VendorContactRole

VendorContactUpdate.description:
Partial update of a contact.

``is_primary`` is not here: promoting a contact demotes another one in the
same transaction, which is an operation rather than a field edit, so it has
its own endpoint.
VendorContactUpdate.title: VendorContactUpdate

VendorCreate.description:
Payload for creating a vendor.

``company_id`` is absent by design: it comes from the authenticated
principal and is never accepted from a client (section 40). So are
``is_approved``, ``approved_by_id``, ``approved_at`` and ``rating`` - a
vendor is created unapproved and unrated, and both are changed only through
their own permission-gated endpoints.
VendorCreate.title: VendorCreate

VendorInvoiceCreate.description: Record a bill in DRAFT. Nothing posts to the ledger until approval.
VendorInvoiceCreate.title: VendorInvoiceCreate

VendorInvoiceLineIn.description:
One billed line.

``taxable_amount``, the tax split and ``line_total`` are computed by the
server from quantity, price, discount and rate - see
``service.price_invoice_line``. Accepting them would let a client post a
line whose parts do not add up, which the CHECK constraints would then
reject with a message nobody can act on.
VendorInvoiceLineIn.title: VendorInvoiceLineIn

VendorInvoiceStatus.description:
Lifecycle of a purchase invoice.

``DISPUTED`` is a live state, not a terminal one: a disputed invoice is
still owed until it is either resolved back to APPROVED or cancelled.
VendorInvoiceStatus.title: VendorInvoiceStatus

VendorInvoiceSummary.description:
List row. Carries the derived outstanding so the payables screen does not
subtract two columns in the browser and disagree with the ageing report.
VendorInvoiceSummary.title: VendorInvoiceSummary

VendorInvoiceUpdate.description:
Amend an invoice that has not been approved.

Replacing ``lines`` replaces the whole set: a bill is a document, and
patching individual lines of a document somebody is about to approve invites
an approval of something other than what was reviewed.
VendorInvoiceUpdate.title: VendorInvoiceUpdate

VendorOption.description:
Slim shape for pickers.

A separate projection rather than :class:`VendorRead`: the picker appears on
every procurement screen and has no use for bank or address details.
VendorOption.title: VendorOption

VendorQualityItemRow.description: One item's contribution to a vendor's rejection rate.
VendorQualityItemRow.title: VendorQualityItemRow

VendorQualitySummary.description:
Rejection rate by vendor, broken down by item.

Consumed by the vendor rating service alongside its own delivery figures.
``has_evidence`` is false when the vendor has no inspected quantity in the
window at all - a distinction the rating engine needs, because "never
rejected anything" and "never delivered anything" are not the same vendor.
VendorQualitySummary.title: VendorQualitySummary

VendorRatingRead.description:
Outcome of a rating computation.

``rating`` is null when the window did not contain enough evidence; the
stored rating is then left untouched, and ``reason`` says why.
VendorRatingRead.title: VendorRatingRead

VendorRatingRequest.description:
Parameters for a rating recomputation.

Deliberately carries no performance figures. The metrics are read from
goods receipts and QC inspections on the server; accepting them from the
client would let a buyer type their own vendor's score.
VendorRatingRequest.title: VendorRatingRequest

VendorRead.description:
Full vendor representation.

``bank_account_number`` is returned masked. The full number is needed only
by the payment run, which reads the row directly; every screen that merely
displays a vendor gets the last four digits, so a shoulder-surfed browser
tab is not a payment-diversion starting point.
VendorRead.title: VendorRead

VendorType.description:
What we buy from a vendor. A vendor may hold several of these at once.

A *classification*, not a permission: no rule reads it to decide whether an
operation is legal. It drives the vendor picker on each document type (a
job-work order proposes JOB_WORK vendors first) and the procurement spend
reports.
VendorType.title: VendorType

VendorUpdate.description:
Partial update of a vendor.

``code`` is not updatable: it is quoted on purchase orders and vendor-portal
URLs, so renaming it in place invalidates history that has already left the
building. Retire the vendor and create the replacement instead.

Approval and rating are absent for the same reason as on create - they have
their own endpoints and their own permissions.
VendorUpdate.title: VendorUpdate

WarehouseCreate.description:
Payload for creating a warehouse.

``company_id`` is absent by design: it comes from the authenticated
principal's tenant context and is never accepted from a client (section 40).

allow_negative_stock.description: Relaxes the inventory pre-flight availability check for this warehouse only. The database still forbids negative on-hand stock. Enable only for warehouses where receipts are legitimately posted after issues, such as line-side WIP.
allow_negative_stock.title: Allow Negative Stock

WarehouseCreate.title: WarehouseCreate

WarehouseOption.description:
Slim shape for pickers and dropdowns.

A dedicated projection rather than ``WarehouseRead``: the picker is called on
nearly every document screen and does not need the address block.
WarehouseOption.title: WarehouseOption

WarehouseType.description:
The stock-holding roles a warehouse can play (master rules section 9).

This is a *classification*, not a permission: no rule reads it to decide
whether a movement is legal - that is what the item capability flags and the
stock-state vocabulary are for. It drives defaults (where a GRN proposes to
receive), reporting groups, and the shop-floor pickers.
WarehouseType.title: WarehouseType

WarehouseUpdate.description:
Partial update. Only the keys present in the request are applied.

``code`` is intentionally not updatable: it is printed on labels, quoted in
document references and used by integrations, so renaming it in place would
invalidate history that has already left the building. Retire the warehouse
and create the replacement instead.
WarehouseUpdate.title: WarehouseUpdate

WhereUsedRead.description: One parent that consumes the queried component.
WhereUsedRead.title: WhereUsedRead

WipOrderRow.description: One live job, as the planner's board shows it.
WipOrderRow.title: WipOrderRow

WipWorkCentreRow.description: Load on one work centre, from the work orders currently on it.
WipWorkCentreRow.title: WipWorkCentreRow

WorkCenterUpdate.description: Partial update. Only the keys actually sent are applied.
WorkCenterUpdate.title: WorkCenterUpdate

WorkOrderUpdate.description: Assignment and scheduling. Quantities move through bookings, never here.
WorkOrderUpdate.title: WorkOrderUpdate

src__modules__allocation__schemas__Relea.description:
Give back part or all of a reservation.

``quantity`` omitted means "release whatever is left", which is what
cancelling a demand document does. A number releases exactly that much and
leaves the rest standing.
src__modules__allocation__schemas__Relea.title: ReleaseRequest

src__modules__assembly__schemas__Complet.description:
Report the output of an assembly run.

``assembled_quantity`` and ``rejected_quantity`` both consumed components:
a lock set that failed final inspection ate its cylinder just as a good one
did. Their sum is what the consumption is scaled from.
src__modules__assembly__schemas__Complet.title: CompleteRequest

src__modules__assembly__schemas__QcResul.description:
The inspection verdict on an assembly's held output.

The two quantities must account for everything on hold: releasing part of a
held lot and leaving the rest in limbo is how stock becomes permanently
unusable without anybody deciding that it should be.
src__modules__assembly__schemas__QcResul.title: QcResultRequest

src__modules__assembly__schemas__ReasonR.description: The payload every state transition shares: why it happened.
src__modules__assembly__schemas__ReasonR.title: ReasonRequest

src__modules__bom__schemas__CopyAsNewVer.description: Create the next version of a BOM from an existing one.
src__modules__bom__schemas__CopyAsNewVer.title: CopyAsNewVersionRequest

src__modules__customers__schemas__Status.description:
Reason capture for a lifecycle change.

Required, not optional: section 83 is explicit that a state change with no
recorded reason is what makes an audit trail useless six months later, when
nobody remembers why an account was switched off.
src__modules__customers__schemas__Status.title: StatusChangeRequest

src__modules__dispatch__schemas__ReasonR.description: A status change that needs no data beyond why it happened.
src__modules__dispatch__schemas__ReasonR.title: ReasonRequest

src__modules__inventory__schemas__Reason.description: A mandatory reason for an irreversible action (section 83).
src__modules__inventory__schemas__Reason.title: ReasonRequest

src__modules__job_work__schemas__QcResul.description:
The inspection verdict on a job work order's held output.

Stated per output item, always. An order that sent three castings out for
three different finishes holds three different item codes, and a single
accepted/rejected pair could only be split between them by guessing - which
would release stock of one code and damage stock of another.

The verdict must account for everything on hold: releasing part of a held lot
and leaving the rest in limbo is how stock becomes permanently unusable
without anybody deciding that it should be.
src__modules__job_work__schemas__QcResul.title: QcResultRequest

src__modules__job_work__schemas__ReasonR.description: The payload every state transition shares: why it happened.
src__modules__job_work__schemas__ReasonR.title: ReasonRequest

src__modules__organization__schemas__Rea.description:
Reason capture for a lifecycle change.

Required, not optional: a state change with no recorded reason is what makes
an audit trail useless six months later, when nobody remembers why a branch
was switched off (section 83).
src__modules__organization__schemas__Rea.title: ReasonRequest

src__modules__packing__schemas__Complete.description:
Finish packing.

``allow_short_pack`` is the deliberate escape hatch for a shipment that goes
out incomplete. It is off by default so the ordinary case cannot silently
ship less than the customer ordered, and it is recorded in the audit entry
when it is used.

* Authentication is a bearer access token; refresh tokens rotate on use.

get.description:
One row per party and denomination in one aggregate query. Payables are aged from the invoice due date. Receivables have no invoice document in this schema, so they are netted out of the ledger oldest-first and aged from the posting date.

There is no exchange-rate table in this schema, so nothing here is summed across denominations. The response carries one block per currency the company has an open item in, and `currencies[0]` - the block whose figures are also restated at the top level - is `currency` if you asked for one, otherwise the company's own currency if anything is open in it, and failing that the currency with the most open documents. Blocks are ordered by open-document count, never by amount: two denominations cannot be compared by size without a rate this schema does not hold. Asking for nothing therefore returns the whole book, never an empty page.

`limit` is parties per denomination; each block reports `party_count` so a capped block is visible as capped, and its totals are the whole block's either way.
